subject: Evidence request: export controls, KMS origin & least-privilege mapping for DPA annex
messages:
From: Anna Müller <anna.muller@finbank.de>

Cc: LegalOps <legalops@finbank.de>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Evidence request for DPA annex - KMS origin, exports, and access mapping

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and infosec teams have a couple of follow-ups as we move toward signing the DPA annex. Can you please provide the following:

1) Confirmation of KMS origin and whether customer data encryption keys are exportable outside of the EU (we need evidence for our export-control review).
2) A least-privilege mapping for all roles that can access raw PII (Redwood engineers, SREs, support).
3) A current list of subprocessors with clear regional data residency notes (which subprocessors may process EU-origin data).
4) Data-flow diagram (high level) showing how PII moves from ingestion through model inference, caching, and logs; note where pseudonymization/aggregation occurs.

We will treat this as an evidence package for our privacy assessment. If you can attach any existing artifacts (diagram, key-policy summary, SOC2 exhibits) that would be ideal.

Best,
Anna
Anna Müller
Senior Privacy Manager, FinBank AG

- KMS origin: keys for customer data are provisioned in the customer's region by default; for our hosted EU customers keys are created in the EU region KMS. We do not export raw customer keys off-region by default.
- Subprocessors: we have an up-to-date subprocessor register (I'll attach).
- Dataflow: Marissa will assemble a redacted diagram and a short narrative that calls out where PII is retained vs transient caches.

We'll aim to have the initial package to you by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-18). If anything else is urgent, flag it and we'll prioritize.

Subject: Re: Evidence request for DPA annex - KMS origin, exports, and access mapping

Anna — attaching the requested materials and a short summary below. See attachments: rb_map_network_dataflow_v3.png (redacted), kms_key_policy_summary.txt, and a current subprocessor list included in the DPA pdf.

Summary answers (high level):
- KMS origin & export: For EU tenant data, keys are generated and stored in the EU KMS cluster. Keys are HSM-backed (Cloud KMS/HSM depending on customer choice). Key material is not exported or escrowed outside the EU by default. Customers can request a key export under explicit contract terms; such exports require approval and are logged.

- Least-privilege access mapping: role-based access controls (RBAC) apply. Engineers have scoped access to model runtime debug logs (obfuscated by default); only senior SREs on-call and security engineers have access to trace-level logs that could contain transient PII, and that access is time-bound and audited. See the short table in kms_key_policy_summary.txt for mapping.

- Subprocessors & residency: list in DPA_Annex_A_redwood_v1.pdf. Short note: inference GPU fleet (managed) runs in region-specific clusters; caching nodes are region-local unless customer opts into multi-region replication.

Attached: rb_map_network_dataflow_v3.png (redacted diagram) — it shows ingestion -> parsing -> ephemeral KV cache (TTL 30m) -> inference runtime -> response; permanent storage only contains minimal audit logs and metrics (no raw request payloads unless customer enables logging).

Let us know any specific artifacts you need (signed key-policy attestation, SOC2 control numbers, or a DMARC-style log extract).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: rb_map_network_dataflow_v3.png, kms_key_policy_summary.txt, DPA_Annex_A_redwood_v1.pdf]

1) Can you provide a short attestation (signed) that no KMS key material for EU tenants is ever exported outside the EU under your standard operations?
2) For the least-privilege mapping, we need the specific role names and the audit log sample showing a time-bound access event (redacted).
3) Subprocessors: please call out any third parties that process telemetry or logs derived from requests (even if logs are redacted/aggregated).

If you can’t provide the attestation, we may need to escalate to legal for a standard export-control addendum.

Best,
Anna

Subject: Re: Evidence request for DPA annex - KMS origin, exports, and access mapping

Anna — adding a technical response to the attestation & logs ask. Short answers:

- KMS export: Our default operational model uses provider-managed HSM-backed keys that are region-scoped (for EU customers the key material resides in EU HSM). We do not configure cross-region key replication for customer encryption keys. Exports are technically possible only when customer requests key material export (e.g., BYOK scenarios) and that operation requires explicit customer action and legal approval; those operations generate an immutable audit trail in our key-management logs. We can produce a developer-signed attestation template and redactable audit samples.

- Audit/sample: attached is kms_key_policy_summary.txt (which lists the audit log retention, syslog identifiers, and role ids). Example audit events include:
  - 2026-07-31T11:03:22Z | KEY_OP:EXPORT_REQUEST | user:kms-admin-03 | status:REJECTED
  - 2026-06-02T04:12:09Z | KEY_OP:ACCESS | user:sre-oncall | object:key-eu-01 | action:GRANT_TEMP

- Telemetry processors: our metrics/telemetry pipeline uses a third-party ingestion queue (IngestCo) and a log-processing partner (LogStream Inc.) to handle metrics and aggregated logs. Neither receives raw request payloads by default — they operate on aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry. They are listed in the subprocessor register attached to the DPA pdf.

If you would like, we can produce: (a) a signed attestation PDF, (b) a redacted audit-log extract showing a time-bound grant, and (c) a minimal SOC2 control mapping for these controls. Let us know which two of the three you prefer first.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
